'''Norman Henry Tolk''' (January 9, 1938 – June 20, 2026) was an American [[physicist]] and musician.

== Life ==
Tolk was born in [[Idaho Falls, Idaho]].<ref name="vanderbilt.edu">{{cite web |title=Norman H. Tolk |url=http://www.vanderbilt.edu/AnS/physics/cv/tolk.html |publisher=Vanderbilt University |accessdate=July 5, 2015}}</ref> He grew up in a [[Mormon]] and Protestant family.<ref name="mormon.org">{{cite web |title=Hi I'm Norman |url=http://www.mormon.org/norman |publisher=Mormon.org |accessdate=July 5, 2015}}</ref> He majored in physics at [[Harvard College]], graduating in 1960, and earned his Ph.D. in atomic physics from [[Columbia University]] in 1966.<ref name="vanderbilt.edu" /> Recently he was a Professor of Physics and Astronomy at [[Vanderbilt University]].<ref name="vanderbilt.edu" /> For all his life Tolk has been a Mormon.<ref name="mormon.org" /> His daughter-in-law is [[Astrid Tuminez|Astrid S. Tuminez]], president of [[Utah Valley University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nelsonmortuary.com/obituaries/jeffrey-tolk |title=Jeffrey Stuart Tolk Obituary (1963 - 2025) |website=nelsonmortuary.com}}</ref> Tolk died on June 20, 2026, at the age of 88.<ref>[https://www.harpethhills.com/obituaries/norman-tolk Norman Henry Tolk]</ref>

== Physics ==
Ever since second grade, Tolk wanted to become a physicist.<ref name="mormon.org" /> After earning his degrees at Columbia and Harvard, he worked at [[Bell Labs|AT&T Bell Laboratories]] in New Jersey. He brought the [[Free-electron laser]] to Vanderbilt. In 1987, he got the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt Award]] and as a result researched at [[Free University of Berlin]].<ref name="vanderbilt.edu" />
